limited.name: nat-pred-frames
limited.basis: Section 5: the image ends at byte 4,664, so F0 = 65,536 and H0 = F0 + 16 MiB = 16,842,752. A cell is 2 header words plus its payload, rounded to a power of two of at least 4 words (check-core's `cell`). Boot pushes Top(0) (3 words, section 6), so top = F0 + 12, and materializes the pool's Big 2^31 + 1 (payload 1: 16 B). main's entry is a tail entry below Top (section 6.2): no Call frame; its Activation (owner, depth and 2 slots: payload 4, 6 words, so 8) is 32 B, so bump = H0 + 48. Eval Let pushes Bind (top F0 + 24); its Return pops it and pushes Scope (F0 + 24). Eval Case selects Succ (section 6.1: selection allocates nothing), pushes Scope(depth), and only then allocates the predecessor 2^31, a Big of 16 B (vm-spec D17: the allocation follows the push). Completed, the run ends at H0 + 64, which check-core's section 5 model (`ceiling_run`) also gives for this plan. With a 24-byte frame region the Case's Scope needs F0 + 36: Exhausted kind 3 (frames) before anything is written, so the predecessor is never made: top = F0 + 24 = 65,560 and bump = H0 + 48 = 16,842,800. A VM that made the predecessor before the push would stop with bump H0 + 64

limited.name: nat-pred-heap
limited.basis: Section 5: the image ends at byte 4,664, so F0 = 65,536 and H0 = F0 + 16 MiB = 16,842,752. A cell is 2 header words plus its payload, rounded to a power of two of at least 4 words (check-core's `cell`). Boot pushes Top(0) (3 words, section 6), so top = F0 + 12, and materializes the pool's Big 2^31 + 1 (payload 1: 16 B). main's entry is a tail entry below Top (section 6.2): no Call frame; its Activation (owner, depth and 2 slots: payload 4, 6 words, so 8) is 32 B, so bump = H0 + 48. Eval Let pushes Bind (top F0 + 24); its Return pops it and pushes Scope (F0 + 24). Eval Case selects Succ (section 6.1: selection allocates nothing), pushes Scope(depth), and only then allocates the predecessor 2^31, a Big of 16 B (vm-spec D17: the allocation follows the push). Completed, the run ends at H0 + 64, which check-core's section 5 model (`ceiling_run`) also gives for this plan. With a 48-byte heap the pool Big and the Activation fill it (a cell may end at HL); the Case's Scope is pushed (top = F0 + 36 = 65,572), and the predecessor's 16 B are Exhausted kind 2 (heap) with bump = H0 + 48 = 16,842,800, as the section 5 model stopped at the heap limit gives. A VM that made the predecessor before the push would stop with top F0 + 24

ceiling.rule: Images whose bump pointer ends within 16 MiB of 4 GiB, where describe used to reserve a 16 MiB text window and a worklist above it in 32-bit arithmetic (review round 2), and, from review round 4, images whose last cell ends exactly at 4 GiB, which section 5 allows (only a cell ending beyond the maximum stops). Provenance: c9869ef chose the first six plans' fill counts a and b by measuring the pre-fix VM's bump pointer, and pinned `bump` from that measurement; review round 3 found it labelled literal review. The gate now derives every row before any VM runs: check-core's `ceiling_run` sums SPEC section 5's cell sizes over the plan (no reclamation, CORE.md choice 1; append as one block, choice 4), stops at a cell that would end beyond 4 GiB with Exhausted kind 2 (heap), and `ceiling_expectation` completes a Program at its Emit and starts a Book's text at the bump pointer (choice 12). Each `expect` and `dump` must equal that derivation; it agrees with every measured pin, so no value changed. The four rows at exactly 4 GiB chose their fill counts from that model alone, before any VM ran them. Each basis records the arithmetic. Each run touches about 4 GiB, so at most two run at a time, each in its own process.

The stdout is literal review: every function returns On, so main is On{} of Res (type 2, tag 1). The pre-fix VM's worklist, based 16 MiB above the text, wrapped onto On's name word, and it printed Evaluated\t2\t1\t{} (review round 2)

rows.name: ceiling-program-top
rows.basis: Section 5 arithmetic (check-core's ceiling_run derives it): H0 = 65,536 + 16 MiB = 16,842,752; the pool's Big 2^31 (16 B) and the SCon of "x" (32 B); a Program (section 8): the terminal continuation, 16 B; then main's Activation of 13 slots (128 B) and ceiling-top's 13 lets with fill1(a = 575,373) and fill2(b = 3), three 64-byte steps fewer and two 48-byte steps more, so they end at 4,294,967,184; main returns the erased Closure of \R. \k. k(Unit), 16 B (node, no captures); phase 1 enters it (an Activation of 0 slots, 16 B), and it returns the live Closure, 16 B; phase 2 enters that with the terminal continuation (an Activation of 1 slot, 32 B), and its Invoke of k allocates Emit{Unit}, 32 B, which ends exactly at 4 GiB, 4,294,967,296. Phase 3 completes with exit 0 and no output, and nothing more is allocated. The reference evaluation (evaluate.program) completes the same plan, with every fill shortened to 3, with exit 0 and no output. The pre-fix VM trapped at Emit's allocation; a VM that stopped a cell ending at 4 GiB would exhaust early (section 11)

reference.rule: Books whose expected run is literal review of the plan under SPEC sections 3 and 6, written before the VM change (D7), and which the gate also compares with vm-spec's reference evaluation (vm/evaluate.py `book`): the frozen run and `calls` must equal the reference's, and the VM's must equal both. Completing Chr{w} reads its operand as the reference's `construct` does (`word`), so a laundered non-scalar is ill-typed there, used or not (CORE.md choice 13; review round 3).
